h1:
Phichit Freshwater Fish
Grilled Fish, Tom Yum & Nan River Dining
intro: Phichit is a town the Nan River runs straight through, so it's no surprise the food it's known for is freshwater fish — from pla kang catfish and pla ma to butter catfish and clown knifefish. The local spots here cook river fish fresh, with the kind of bold, homestyle flavor you don't get anywhere else. These are the fish restaurants Phichit folks actually bring their relatives to, and the dishes worth ordering when you get there.

blocks.html: Phichit isn't a coastal town, but it's a genuine river-fish town. The Nan River flows through Mueang, Taphan Hin, and Bang Mun Nak districts, and people here have been tied to freshwater fish since their grandparents' day. When there's an event or guests come to visit, the dishes Phichit locals reach for first are tom yum fish, grilled fish, and fried fish. The fish used is mostly pla kang (giant river catfish), pla ma (soldier river barb), butter catfish, snakehead, and clown knifefish — each giving firm or sweet flesh that suits a different dish.

We've picked the spots that do freshwater fish well and get talked about across Phichit — restaurants in town with awards to back them up, roadside places drivers stop at on the regular, and riverside spots where you can settle in for the evening. Some may be worth a quick call before you go, since opening days and hours can change.

blocks.text: Phichit Freshwater Fish Restaurants Worth Trying

items.name: Lung Waen River Fish (the original)
items.blurb: A river-fish restaurant in town that Phichit locals rate as one of the province's best, backed by Wongnai user awards over several years. The standouts are tom yum fish with fish roe, fish fried with fish sauce, fried clown knifefish cakes, and choo chee butter catfish — cooked homestyle, big on flavor, with fresh fish that isn't fishy.
items.meta: Sa Luang Rd, Nai Mueang, Mueang Phichit · open roughly 9:00–21:00

items.name: Krua Pla Yai
items.blurb: A roadside spot in the Pho Prathap Chang area known for real river fish, not farmed. The dishes people order most are tom yum pla ma, grilled tilapia, butter catfish fried with garlic, and snakehead stir-fried with Chinese celery. Big bowls and big plates, great value, perfect for coming as a family.
items.meta: Thung Yai, Pho Prathap Chang · open roughly 8:00–20:00 daily

items.name: Te Te River Fish
items.blurb: A river-fish restaurant in the Thap Khlo area focused on several kinds of freshwater fish — pla kang, pla ma, and butter catfish. Favorites to order are fried fish, tom yum fish, and snacks like salted-egg squid. It's a local spot the people around there drop in on regularly.
items.meta: Khao Sai, Thap Khlo · open roughly 9:30–21:00 daily

items.name: Rom Makham (Taphan Hin)
items.blurb: A big restaurant in the Taphan Hin area people have been stopping at for years. The setting is open and easygoing, good for a large table, with a wide range of river fish — tom yum, fried fish, and grilled fish — and bold-flavored dishes in the local style.
items.meta: Huai Ket, Taphan Hin · open roughly 10:00–21:00 daily

items.name: Sabai Bang (Bang Mun Nak)
items.blurb: A laid-back riverside spot in the Bang Mun Nak area serving several kinds of river fish, with a breezy place to sit and eat. It's a good evening choice — order grilled fish and tom yum to share while the air cools down.

items.name: Aharn Pa Krua Pa Lek
items.blurb: A wild-food and river-fish restaurant with friendly prices, serving fish, frog, and other jungle-style dishes done as stir-fries, tom yum, and curries. The flavors are bold and properly seasoned — one for anyone who likes their food spicy.

blocks.title: Tip for ordering fish
blocks.html: The nicer river fish like pla kang or pla ma are often limited per day. If you're set on a big whole-fish dish, call ahead to reserve, or come late morning to midday — you'll get fresher fish and a better pick of sizes than you would in the evening.

blocks.text: Freshwater Fish Dishes to Order When You're in Phichit

blocks.html: If you make it to a Phichit fish restaurant and aren't sure what to get, these are the core dishes nearly every place does well — and a fair measure of the kitchen's skill. Order three or four to share and you'll eat comfortably.

items.name: Tom yum pla kang
items.blurb: The headline dish at Phichit's fish restaurants. Giant river catfish has firm, chewy flesh in a sour-spicy, well-balanced tom yum broth — some places add fish roe to make it richer. It's the plate that tells you whether a restaurant really knows how to cook fish.

items.name: Salt-grilled fish / grilled tilapia
items.blurb: A whole fish stuffed with lemongrass and pandan, then grilled until the skin is crisp and the flesh inside is soft and sweet. Dip it in spicy seafood sauce — it's the dish that pairs best with sticky rice and keeps you going.

items.name: Fried clown knifefish cakes
items.blurb: Clown knifefish scraped, shaped, and fried — bouncy and chewy, fragrant with curry paste. Eat it as a snack or with rice. Plenty of Phichit places make them big and dense.

items.name: Garlic-fried butter catfish
items.blurb: Butter catfish has tender, delicate flesh, fried with garlic until fragrant and crisp outside, soft within. It's an easy one for kids since there aren't many bones.

items.name: Snakehead with Chinese celery / choo chee fish
items.blurb: Snakehead or butter catfish stir-fried with fragrant Chinese celery, or done choo chee style under a rich curry-paste sauce. It's a dish you'll happily go through several plates of rice with.

blocks.text: Why Phichit's Freshwater Fish Is Worth It

blocks.html: Phichit sits in the middle of the Nan River basin, with rivers, marshes, and rice paddies that have raised wild fish for ages. Many local restaurants buy fish straight from area fishermen, so what you get is fresh and varies by season. Phichit cooks tend toward bold, sour-spicy, fully seasoned flavors rather than leading with sweetness — which suits the distinct character of freshwater fish well.

items: Pla kang (giant river catfish) — firm, chewy, rich flesh that suits tom yum and curries; the restaurants' premium fish
Pla ma (soldier river barb) — sweet flesh, popular for tom yum and frying; a Phichit favorite
Butter catfish — tender with few bones, good for garlic-frying or choo chee
Clown knifefish — scraped into bouncy, chewy fried cakes; a regular at the table
Snakehead / tilapia — available year-round and done every way: grilled, fried, and stir-fried

blocks.text: Eating Fish by the Nan River in Phichit

blocks.html: The charm of eating fish in Phichit is the riverside setting. Several restaurants around Taphan Hin and Bang Mun Nak sit close to the Nan River or its side canals, easy places to sit and catch the cool evening breeze — great with family or a group of friends. Order a whole grilled fish, a pot of tom yum, and settle in until the sun drops. If that's the mood you're after, go in the evening and leave the kitchen a little extra time, since whole fish takes longer to cook than the usual dishes.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: Some local fish restaurants are small places with unpredictable closing days or breaks that follow the fishing season. A quick call before you go is the safer bet, especially if you're planning to drive well out of town.

faq.q: Which is the most famous freshwater fish restaurant in Phichit?
faq.a: Lung Waen River Fish (the original) in Mueang Phichit is the one locals rate as the province's best, backed by Wongnai user awards over several years. Its standouts are tom yum fish with fish roe and fried clown knifefish cakes. Outside town there's also Krua Pla Yai in the Pho Prathap Chang area, known for real river fish.

faq.q: What fish dishes should I order in Phichit?
faq.a: Worth trying are tom yum pla kang or tom yum pla ma, salt-grilled fish, fried clown knifefish cakes, and garlic-fried butter catfish. Order three or four to share and you'll be full and get the full range of Phichit freshwater fish.

faq.q: What kinds of fish do Phichit fish restaurants use?
faq.a: Mostly freshwater fish from the Nan River basin — pla kang (giant river catfish), pla ma, butter catfish, clown knifefish, snakehead, and tilapia. Many restaurants buy from local fishermen, and some species are seasonal.

faq.q: Where should I go to eat fish by the Nan River in Phichit?
faq.a: The Taphan Hin and Bang Mun Nak areas have several riverside restaurants, like Rom Makham in Taphan Hin and Sabai Bang in Bang Mun Nak. They're good for an evening sit in the cool breeze with grilled fish and tom yum fish to share.

faq.q: Is fish food in Phichit expensive?
faq.a: Prices are friendly. Most restaurants run around ฿150–500 per person depending on whether you order a big whole fish. Coming as a group and sharing works out better value, since big river fish are made as large plates meant for several people.
